# Mabel Colby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- **Rank:** Sophomore  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)</sub>
- **Role:** keeper of the family financial records  <sub>[v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001)</sub>
- **Titles:** the “rose-red” girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Mabel is a striking, dark-eyed young woman who earned the title of beauty prize winner among the Second Year classes at Regent's Academy.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)_

## Personality

Mabel possesses a contemplative, creative, and dream-filled heart brimming with yearning imaginations. While she can be contemplative and prone to occasional despondency over her studies, she maintains a playful, witty sense of humor, often quoting poetry mockingly or lightheartedly laughing through mournful stories. When writing essays, she is notoriously messy and habitually tosses every completed manuscript page onto the floor.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c16 P40](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0040), [v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031), [v3 c35 P44](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0044), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021)_

## Goals

- to attend college at Wexcombe  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>
- to write a paper detailing the realistic trials of a country schoolteacher  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>

## History

While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel became close friends with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, distinguishing herself among her peers by winning the Second Year beauty prize. Following her time at the Academy, she worked continuously as a schoolteacher in an isolated country school, instructing students across nine grades. Tired of the demanding routine and low public appreciation of country teaching, she resolved to leave her job and pursue higher education. Being eligible for the Sophomore class after completing three years at Regent's, she enrolled at Wexcombe College. She rented a household at Tabby's Place alongside Nell, Honora, and Cressy Lindsay, with her Aunt Euphemia joining them to handle housekeeping while Mabel managed the financial records. Throughout her time at college, she engaged in academic life, wrote papers for the Philomathic Society, shared in house routines, and participated in literary activities like reading Story Club manuscripts with her housemates.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004), [v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001), [v3 c35 P44](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0044), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021)_

## Quotes

> Why on earth aren’t you coming? The grave is prepared by us. ‘What silent still and silent all?’  <sub>[v3 c16 P40](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0040)</sub>

> Is that so?  <sub>[v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001)</sub>

> I am extremely happy that Tabby’s Place remains ours for one more year. My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m feeling down and disheartened too. Nothing appears to have any value. Even my thoughts are ancient. I’ve already pondered every single one. What purpose does life serve anyway, Nell?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—yet I entertain no jealousy. I hold affection for Nell, and Cyril pleases me. Everyone asserts that her marriage will be a splendid one, and at present even Mrs. Lisle finds her delightful. Everything appears as though it were fashioned in paradise, though I harbor my reservations. Take whatever you can from that, Aunt Euphemia.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
